title: n queens by omission-based abstraction
description: The n-queens puzzle with an abstraction that omits constraints (omission-based abstraction, Saribatur and Eiter): the diagonal constraints start switched off, each guarded by an #external atom. A candidate that the full program rejects names the diagonals it breaks, and the loop switches those constraints on (A.set) instead of adding a clause about the candidate. track draws how many of the 4n - 2 diagonal constraints the loop needed. Solutions: all placements (n = 8: 92).

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% n queens on an n x n board. Diagonal D: the up diagonals are numbered R + C (2 .. 2n),
% the down diagonals 2n + R - C + n (2n + 1 .. 4n - 1).
row(1..n).
diag(R,C,R+C) :- row(R), row(C).
diag(R,C,2*n+R-C+n) :- row(R), row(C).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% The abstraction omits the diagonal constraints: one queen per row and per column only.
1 { q(R,C) : row(C) } 1 :- row(R).
1 { q(R,C) : row(R) } 1 :- row(C).
% Each diagonal constraint is guarded by an external atom, false at the start. The loop
% switches one on (A.set) when a candidate breaks it: the refinement puts back an omitted
% part of the program instead of adding a clause about the candidate.
#external active(D) : diag(_,_,D).
:- active(D), #count { R,C : q(R,C), diag(R,C,D) } > 1.
#show q/2.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: the full program says no. violated(D): two queens on diagonal D.
violated(D) :- diag(R1,C1,D), diag(R2,C2,D), q(R1,C1), q(R2,C2), R1 < R2.
bad :- violated(_).
:- not bad.
#show violated/1.

fragments.name: check_clause
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: the full program says no. violated(D): two queens on diagonal D.
violated(D) :- diag(R1,C1,D), diag(R2,C2,D), q(R1,C1), q(R2,C2), R1 < R2.
bad :- violated(_).
:- not bad.
#show violated/1.
% Variant clauses: the queens on a broken diagonal are relevant; one of them must move.
relevant(q(R,C)) :- violated(D), diag(R,C,D), q(R,C).
fragments.description: The check with relevant/1, for the variant clauses.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Omission-based abstraction (Saribatur and Eiter): the abstraction is the program with some
# constraints left out. A candidate that the full program rejects shows which omitted
# constraints matter; they are put back (A.set of an external atom), and the abstraction
# keeps no clause about the candidate itself. Only the diagonals that some candidate broke
# are ever switched on.
active = 0
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        for v in X.atoms(violated/1):
            A.set(A.atom("active", v.arg(1)), true)
            active = active + 1
        track constraints = active
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The blocking loop: no diagonal is ever switched on; every bad placement is blocked.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Switch on only one broken diagonal per counterexample.
active = 0
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        for v in X.atoms(violated/1):
            A.set(A.atom("active", v.arg(1)), true)
            active = active + 1
            break
        track constraints = active
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Plain CEGAR instead of omission: a clause per counterexample (one of the queens on a broken
# diagonal moves); no diagonal is switched on.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

generators.name: given
generators.description: k queens given in rows 1..k (random distinct columns, no two on a diagonal) on an n x n board; set the instance constant n to the same value.
generators.text:
% given: queens in rows 1..k at the columns of a random permutation of 1..n, redrawn if two share a diagonal
q(R,@perm(n, R, cols)) :- R = 1..k.
:- q(R1,C1), q(R2,C2), R1 < R2, R2 - R1 = |C2 - C1|.
#show q/2.

library.summary: n queens by omission-based abstraction: the diagonal constraints start switched off (#external) and are switched on (A.set) when a candidate breaks them (n = 8, 92 solutions).
